PAGASA reports show yesterday’s peak at 28.5 °C, with today’s forecast centering on 29 °C amid continued monsoon flow. These conditions—high humidity, reduced insolation, and frequent precipitation—favor outcomes clustered around 28–30 °C rather than higher readings typical of clearer August days. eventMetadata.context_description: Forecasts for Mexico City on August 14 center on a daily maximum of 24–26°C amid the city's highland elevation of roughly 2,240 meters and peak rainy-season conditions. Persistent cloud cover, afternoon convection, and scattered showers or thunderstorms—driven by monsoon moisture and orographic lift—limit surface heating and cap peak temperatures near the long-term August average of 24°C. Model runs show minor divergence in timing and intensity of precipitation, which can shift the observed high by 1–2°C depending on how much solar radiation reaches the surface before storms develop. Trader consensus clusters tightly around these outcomes because current guidance lacks strong signals for either unusual clear skies or heavy suppression, with resolution hinging on the precise maximum recorded by official stations before any evening cooling.
